A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GF-DRO research. Their text, equations, figures, algorithms, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, sampling, CIFAR-10 feature robustness, and uncertain least-squares experiments in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original MNIST and CIFAR-10 CNN evaluations, facial-image sampling examples, and supplementary diagnostics.

M1.justification: The stated sampler procedures change substantially: WGF/WFR drift signs and WFR reaction signs are reversed; Algorithm 4 replaces weight-proportional rejuvenation with uniform selection excluding the dying particle; Algorithm 5 adds the negative 2τ/ϵ score factor and the missing stepsize multiplier. These affect actual update rules, although the PDFs do not establish corresponding code changes or reruns.

E1.justification: v3 adds MNIST digit classification, FFHQ latent-space facial-attribute sampling, and raw-image CIFAR-10 adversarial evaluation alongside the retained fixed-feature task. L∞ attacks supplement L2 evaluation. The earlier synthetic classification and least-squares coverage remains in Appendix D.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained experiments preserve their comparator membership, including WRM, Dual Sinkhorn DRO, SAA/ERM, and the relevant sampler variants. The new CNN comparisons reuse existing methods. Newly cited works, including Wang (2025), are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce end-to-end LeNet-5 training and ResNet-18 fine-tuning, distinct PGD attack grids, and controlled latent-space sampling. The ResNet-18 comparison specifies 20 epochs, batch size 256, eight particles, and 20 inner steps at stepsize 0.01. These are added protocols; the retained CIFAR-10 feature experiment still uses 10 epochs and 100 inner iterations.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained entropy and SVG-initialization analyses, v3 adds facial-sampling ablations over τ, ϵ, stepsize, and particle count, plus trajectories illustrating instability and convergence. Appendix D.3 adds CNN training-loss diagnostics and an MNIST τ-sensitivity comparison.

E5.justification: v1 reports no empirical run counts or uncertainty estimates. v3 introduces mean ± standard deviation robustness tables, explicitly reports five seeds for CIFAR-10 and five runs for convergence diagnostics, and supplies timing uncertainty. This does not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial quantitative and qualitative results while retaining the earlier benchmark plots. For example, new Table 4 reports CIFAR-10 PGD-L∞ error at Δ=0.015 of 34.06±0.83% for WFR-DRO, 35.02±1.13% for WGF-DRO, 39.74±1.86% for Dual, and 86.35±1.57% for WRM. Timing, sensitivity, and facial-sampling findings are also new; these are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The outer-iteration bound changes from O(ϵ_opt^-2) to O(ϵ_opt^-4), with an S-dependent stepsize; Appendix C.4 changes total accuracy dependence from ϵ_opt^-4 to ϵ_opt^-6. Proposition 4.2 revises assumptions and gives an expected gradient-error bound for sufficiently large N, with explicit particle-approximation error. Important inconsistencies persist or arise: Theorem 5.5 states dimension dependence d whereas C.4 derives d², and the revised main-text Gibbs exponent omits the 2τ factor retained in C.1.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unified gradient-flow sampling framework for existing DRO problems, sampler-based solvers, and recovery of WRM as a special case. v3 foregrounds non-convex neural-network applicability, but v1 already allowed non-concave losses and analyzed non-convex optimization. The underlying contribution scope remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of intermediate-flow selection under poor hyperparameters, facial-sample diversity and failure conditions, and CNN optimization behavior. It also discusses possible extensions beyond smoothness and leaves analysis of an SGDA-style variant to future work. The earlier WFR warm-start and RGO applicability limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds ResNet-18 architectural adaptations, optimizer and training hyperparameters, MLMC truncation settings, latent-sampler configurations, controlled ablation settings, and measured training times. These materially expand reproducibility information. The stated RTX A3000 hardware and code-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting entropic JKO, nonsmooth ULA, PGD, and latent autoencoders, and acknowledges Wang (2025) for identifying a proof flaw. Comparisons with FlowDRO and iterative JKO approaches become more explicit, while the basic positioning as a complementary sampling framework remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and discussion are substantially rewritten, and the main experimental narrative is rebuilt around CNNs and facial sampling. Earlier main-text experiments move into Appendix D, WFR details move into a dedicated Appendix B.1, and definitions, terminology, and explanations are reorganized.

P2.justification: v3 adds a framework diagram, facial trajectory and ablation panels, a CNN convergence plot, and six tables covering robustness, timing, and sensitivity. The eight earlier figures are retained but rearranged within Appendix D. Algorithm placement and the visual organization of the main text also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The new end-to-end evaluations, uncertainty reporting, and sensitivity/timing analyses substantially strengthen support for practical applicability beyond v1's toy and fixed-feature studies. Revised sampler updates and the variance-aware outer-loop rate also address important defects. These gains outweigh the revised theory's consistency problems, including conflicting target scaling between Section 3 and Appendix C.1 and conflicting dimension dependence between Theorem 5.5 and Appendix C.4. The theory should therefore not be regarded as fully repaired.
